This contract      reads them back through the HyperCore read precompiles, synchronously and without an external feed:      the values match the latest HyperCore state at the time the EVM block was constructed.Not an `IYieldSourceOracle`: a perp leg is signed, mark-to-market, USD-denominated and per-perp, so      there is no scalar price-per-share to report. It is a structured snapshot \u2014 raw legs plus HyperCore's      own account-level margin summary \u2014 for an off-chain or execution-phase consumer (OMS / strategy      snapshot / hook) to classify and net. NOT for the ERC-4337 validation phase (see the interface).HYPEREVM ONLY (chain 999, testnet 998). Zero storage, no constructor, no events. On any other chain      the precompile addresses are code-less and every read reverts `PRECOMPILE_BAD_RETURN(addr, 0)`: the      oracle fails closed rather than reporting zeros.An unknown perp index makes the precompile fail and consume the gas forwarded to it; the library caps      that at `PRECOMPILE_GAS_LIMIT` per read, so a reverting snapshot costs at most one cap on top of the      reads that succeeded, and refuses (`INSUFFICIENT_GAS`) callers that cannot fund the cap, so a clamped      read is never mistaken for an unknown index. There is no try/catch inside the oracle. Gas envelope:      roughly 27k for the account level plus ~55k per REQUESTED perp (four reads, cold access, decoding;      duplicates are re-read, not cached), so a snapshot of a few dozen perps fits a HyperEVM small block      (3M gas); whole-universe sweeps are `eth_call` only.","errors":{"INSUFFICIENT_GAS(uint256,uint256)":[{"params":{"available":"Gas left at the check","required":"`MIN_CALLER_GAS`"}}],"PRECOMPILE_BAD_RETURN(address,uint256)":[{"details":"Length 0 is the wrong-chain signature: on a chain without HyperCore the fixed addresses are code-less      and a staticcall to them \"succeeds\" with nothing. getAccountSnapshot(address,uint32[]).details: Equivalent to `getAccountSnapshotOnDex(account, 0, perps)`. Rows map 1:1 onto `perps` (no      de-duplication, no reordering). An empty `perps` is allowed and returns only the account-level fields.      Any invalid index fails the WHOLE call — no partial snapshot.

params.account: The account whose positions are read
params.perps: The perp indices the caller covers (the covered universe)

returns.snapshot: Account-level figures and one row per requested perp — never netted

getAccountSnapshotOnDex(address,uint32,u.details: Builder-deployed (HIP-3) dexes keep separate margin: pass the dex the requested legs live on      (`perp / 10000`) so `accountValue`, `marginUsed`, `ntlPos` and `rawUsd` describe them. An unknown      `perpDex` fails the whole call (`PRECOMPILE_CALL_FAILED` from 0x80F). `withdrawableUsd` stays dex 0.

params.account: The account whose positions are read
params.perpDex: The perp dex whose margin summary is reported (0 = native)
params.perps: The perp indices the caller covers

returns.snapshot: Account-level figures on `perpDex` and one row per requested perp — never netted

getPerpPosition(address,uint32).details: STRICT, NO FALLBACK: a zero account reverts `ZERO_ADDRESS`; an unknown perp index makes the precompile      fail and the call reverts `PRECOMPILE_CALL_FAILED`; malformed or empty returndata (wrong chain)      reverts `PRECOMPILE_BAD_RETURN`. Nothing degrades to a zero-valued leg. A perp the account never      traded returns a zero-size row, not a revert.

params.account: The account whose position is read (its own HyperCore master)

returns.position: The raw leg plus the prices and decimals needed to value it

PERP_DEX().notice: Default perp dex for `getAccountSnapshot` (echoed as `AccountSnapshot.perpDex`). 0 is Hyperliquid's         native perp dex; `getAccountSnapshotOnDex` takes the dex explicitly.

getAccountSnapshot(address,uint32[]).notice: Read HyperCore's account-level margin figures on the native perp dex (0) and the legs for `perps`.

getAccountSnapshotOnDex(address,uint32,u.notice: Read HyperCore's account-level margin figures on `perpDex` and the legs for `perps`.
